source.title: AND: Audio Network Dissection for Interpreting Deep Acoustic Models
source.authors: Tung-Yu Wu; Yu-Xiang Lin; T. Weng

record.tranche_reason: The study measures neuron interpretability and polysemanticity in audio models using a clustering-based criterion, rather than testing superposition geometry or capacity competition in toy networks.
record.gate_note: The study measures layer-wise neuron interpretability and reports how it varies with training strategy, which bears on V3. Its concept-specific pruning, classification accuracy, and last-layer dissection comparisons do not test the listed claim versions and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its 'polysemanticity' is an operational uninterpretability score: a neuron counts as uninterpretable if fewer than τ of its top-K audio captions share a K-means sentence cluster. That score depends on the captioner, the LLM and the clustering. The study never mentions superposition or capacity and never varies width or feature count. It compares training strategies only, so it cannot show polysemanticity arising with or without capacity pressure (V2/V3). It covers no toy models (V1), no LLMs or SAEs (V4/V5) and no feature dimensionality (V6). The findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors conclude that training strategy affects neuron interpretability: supervised training narrows neurons' responsive features in deeper layers, while SSL pretraining keeps neurons diverse ('polysemantic'). They say SSL pretraining mitigates the diverse-to-accordant trend in BEATs-finetuned, while whole-model supervised fine-tuning pushes deeper layers toward convergence. Fine-tuning does not mitigate the diversity. They also conclude that the models rely on combinations of basic acoustic features rather than high-level concepts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LLM-generated audio descriptions and sentence clustering to measure neuron interpretability in audio models, rather than the original toy-network superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported percentage of polysemantic neurons varies with the threshold τ and top-K selection; the authors say the broad trends persist across the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In audio transformers, the share of neurons whose top-activating clips lack a shared caption cluster depends on training strategy. Supervised AST falls from shallow to deep layers. SSL BEATs-frozen stays flat. BEATs-finetuned is intermediate. These trends hold across τ and top-K settings, and partly on GTZAN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training objective (supervised vs self-supervised) shapes layer-wise neuron polysemanticity, as measured by description-based interpretability, in acoustic models.

record.problems: The polysemanticity measure is operationalized through LLM-generated audio descriptions and clustering, rather than direct feature or representation geometry. The results do not isolate capacity pressure or establish that it is absent. The principal layer-wise results are shown in figures without exact numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Per-layer plotted values for Figures 6 and 14 were not extracted as individual rows; the record captures the trends explicitly described in the text and the stated GTZAN aggregate bound.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
Capacity competition and dedicated versus shared dimensions are not examined.
No manipulation or argument about capacity pressure. Training-strategy differences alone do not show polysemanticity without capacity pressure.
Audio transformers only; no distributed-feature or SAE analysis in LLMs.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a methods paper (AND, an audio neuron dissection framework). It does not cite Toy Models of Superposition. The pruning, last-layer dissection and human-evaluation results concern method quality and correctly stay out of the rows. The reader's V3 link conflated an interpretability score varying with training with polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, sparse-feature overload, feature directions, sparsity-dependent transition, or geometric regularity are tested.
The study does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity, whether important features receive dedicated dimensions, or whether other features share dimensions.

The study relates training strategy to its measure of neuron interpretability, but does not manipulate or quantify capacity pressure, establish that polysemanticity occurs without capacity pressure, or test other proposed causes.
The study concerns audio models, not LLM feature representations; it does not measure features distributed across neurons or features recovered by an SAE.
No SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status is tested.
The study does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

rows.subject: AST
rows.operation_detail: Measured the percentage of neurons classified as uninterpretable using clustered audio-description sentences.

conditions.value: percentage of uninterpretable neurons by transformer block

rows.measure: Percentage of uninterpretable neurons across transformer blocks
rows.note: The authors state that AST's uninterpretable-neuron percentage decreases from shallow to deep blocks, and interpret this as neurons gradually concentrating on certain concepts. The figure gives layer-wise values.
rows.check: Measures the caption-cluster uninterpretability rate by layer for supervised AST. It says nothing about whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure, so it should not be linked to V3. The 'observed' state has no version effect to refer to.

rows.subject: BEATs-finetuned
rows.stage_stated: self-supervised pretraining with whole-model supervised fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Measured the percentage of neurons classified as uninterpretable using clustered audio-description sentences.

conditions.value: percentage of uninterpretable neurons by transformer block

rows.measure: Percentage of uninterpretable neurons across transformer blocks
rows.note: The authors say whole-model fine-tuning mitigates the diverse-to-accordant trend and describe fine-tuning as guiding the model toward narrower attention. Layer-wise values are plotted.
rows.check: Same construct, for BEATs-finetuned. The authors say SSL pretraining mitigates the shallow-to-deep decline, not that fine-tuning does. 'Partial' has no version referent.

rows.subject: BEATs-frozen
rows.stage_stated: self-supervised pretraining with final linear layer fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Measured the percentage of neurons classified as uninterpretable using clustered audio-description sentences.

conditions.value: percentage of uninterpretable neurons by transformer block

rows.measure: Percentage of uninterpretable neurons across transformer blocks
rows.note: The authors state that the percentage is consistent across layers and interpret this as diverse neuron abilities associated with self-supervised pretraining. Layer-wise values are plotted.
rows.check: Same construct, for BEATs-frozen. Its transformer layers were never trained on ESC50, only the final linear layer was. The flat profile reflects the pretrained SSL weights. The row is not linkable to V3.

rows.subject: AST, BEATs-finetuned, and BEATs-frozen (aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: Applied the neuron-interpretability criterion on the GTZAN Music Genre dataset.
rows.measure: Percentage of neurons classified as uninterpretable
rows.value: No more than 20% for the models
rows.note: The text reports this aggregate bound and says the simpler dataset makes neuron behavior more explainable. It does not state separate values for each model.
rows.check: The aggregate bound on GTZAN ('no more than 20%' uninterpretable at τ=4) is not a test of any version. The text adds that τ=5 gives a clearer trend matching ESC50; the row omits this.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study reports polysemanticity-related variation across training strategies: AST's uninterpretable-neuron rate falls across depth, while BEATs-frozen's remains consistent; see r1 and r3.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ESC50; BEATs-finetuned, and GTZAN at τ = 4
reader_labels.reason: The layer-wise trend is described as mitigated for BEATs-finetuned, and the GTZAN result reports no more than 20% uninterpretable neurons at the stated threshold; see r2 and r4.
